title: VATS-targetable grenades always show 0% hit chance on PC
status: runtime causality proven / chance-formula root cause pending
platform: PC; reported working on Xbox 360 and PS3
summary: Thrown projectiles marked VATS-targetable can be selected, but their computed chance is exactly 0.0, which the VATS menu treats as unqueueable (0% shown, click blocked).
measured: VATS menu gate: at 0x007EEA2D the selected entry's chance field (entry+0x28) is read; if it equals 0.0, 0x007EEA5B displays sVATSMessageZeroChance and the attack cannot be queued. The airborne grenade entry's chance is exactly 0.0 (not a rounded display value). RUNTIME PROOF: writing 0.5 to the selected entry's chance field (selected+0x28) while VATS was open changed the display to 50% and unblocked the queue - single-field causality confirmed. The initial +0x124 max-range hypothesis was falsified: FUN_00646F50 reads the equipped weapon's max range, not the airborne grenade projectile's range.
root_cause_pending: The chance FORMULA for airborne grenade targets returns exactly 0.0. The formula inputs (distance term, skill term, or a thrown-weapon classification branch) must be traced to find which input is zero on PC and nonzero on console.
fix_direction: Stewie's Tweaks 'Allow targeting projectiles in VATS' applies a distance-and-skill-based percentage to grenade targets - confirming the vanilla formula returns 0 by omission, not by a corrupted value. The vanilla fix is to give grenade targets the same distance+skill chance computation that actors receive.

sources.label: Runtime causality proof
sources.detail: selected+0x28 := 0.5 while VATS open -> 50% displayed, queue unblocked

sources.label: Falsified hypothesis
sources.detail: FUN_00646F50 (+0x124 max-range) is weapon range, not projectile range - irrelevant to this bug

falsification_trail.hypothesis: FUN_00646F50 (+0x124 weapon max range) controls the displayed chance
falsification_trail.result: FALSIFIED by runtime patch — returning 500.0 changed nothing
falsification_trail.lesson: FUN_00646F50 is the equipped weapon's max-range accessor, not the projectile range

falsification_trail.hypothesis: FUN_00646F70 (VATS target resolver with grenade branch + 'destructible/grenade target chance' debug string) computes the displayed chance
falsification_trail.result: FALSIFIED by static analysis — zero direct callers, zero data references in the entire image; the function is dead code on PC (likely an Xbox/debug-build chance calculator)
falsification_trail.lesson: Runtime patch (return 1.0 always) also changed nothing — confirming the function never executes

falsification_trail.hypothesis: The zero-chance gate at 0x007EEA46 controls queueing
falsification_trail.result: PATCH APPLIED (test ah,0x44 -> test ah,0x00) but targeting still blocked
falsification_trail.lesson: The displayed 0% itself is what blocks targeting — the fix must change the computed chance value, not the gate

next: 1. Dump the live VATS entry object from memory (menu global 0x011DB0D4 -> +0x100 -> entry); read its vtable pointer and decode the entry class RTTI. 2. The entry class methods include the chance computation/writer. 3. VATSMenu subsystem spans 0x7E9000-0x7F7000 (255 refs to menu global 0x011DB0D4). 4. Atlas PC<->Xbox comparison once the writer is found. 5. Runtime experiment from the protocol remains the closure gate.

title: iSneakLevelBonus can invert the intended sneak modifier
summary: When the player is above an actor's level, the level modifier can become negative and make sneaking harder. GECKWiki points directly at engine address 0x642ED0. YUP has documented the behavior and ultimately reverted its own gamesetting workaround because the underlying calculation remains bugged for some actors.
hypothesis: Signed arithmetic or ordering around the level-difference multiplication allows the bonus term to become a penalty.
next: Decompile 0x642ED0 and its enclosing detection function, map the gamesetting read, reproduce with controlled actor/player levels, then test a minimal arithmetic patch.

title: RemoveAllItems / RemoveAllTypedItems skip normal unequip lifecycle
summary: GECKWiki reports that mass-removal commands do not execute OnUnequip blocks and can leave effects behind. Older modder reports also describe partially removed equipped armor and corrupted inventory state.
hypothesis: The bulk-removal path bypasses the normal equipment teardown routine or removes stack entries before the unequip/event path can observe them.
next: Locate vanilla command handlers and compare their equipped-item branch against UnequipItem/RemoveItem. Build a minimal scripted armor with observable OnUnequip/effect state for reproduction.

title: NPC armor enchantments stack again every time the NPC loads
summary: GECKWiki reports that enchantments on NPC-worn armor can be reapplied on each load and stack indefinitely.
hypothesis: Actor load/equipment restoration reapplies the armor effect without checking for an existing equivalent active effect or without restoring the effect as recovered state.
next: Create an NPC with a measurable armor enchant, cycle unload/reload repeatedly, log actor values, then trace armor restoration and magic-effect application calls.

title: Actor templates in leveled lists are selected disproportionately often
platform: New Vegas; reported working in Fallout 3
summary: GECKWiki reports that if an actor template is itself in a leveled list, it is almost always chosen. The Fallout 3 comparison makes this another useful engine-differential target.
hypothesis: The New Vegas leveled-actor selection path treats template entries differently during eligibility filtering or random weighting.
next: Build a controlled LVLC/LVLN test with equal-weight template and non-template candidates, gather selection frequencies, then trace the leveled actor picker and compare against Fallout 3/Xbox evidence where available.

title: AI packages fail to process correctly while the player is away
platform: New Vegas; reported working in Fallout 3
summary: Sleep, find, patrol and eat packages may fail to advance unless the player enters the cell, crosses a load door, or fast-travels, even when low-level processing should apply.
hypothesis: New Vegas selects the wrong process level or skips package ticks for unloaded actors under some package categories.
next: Construct deterministic patrol/sleep actors with timestamps, compare same-cell and off-cell progress, identify process-level selection and package scheduler functions.

title: Combat / CAUTION state can remain stuck after threats are gone
summary: Combat or caution may persist after moving to a cell with no alerted actors or after enemies die; GECKWiki marks this as only partially fixed by JohnnyGuitar.
hypothesis: One or more detection/combat participants remain registered or a global/player combat-state aggregate is not invalidated on unload/death transitions.
next: Verify behavior with current JohnnyGuitar installed and without it, isolate the remaining reproduction case, then trace player combat-state aggregation and actor removal callbacks.

title: GameMode scripts on crafted items do not run until drop + pickup
summary: GECKWiki reports that crafted scripted items do not begin running GameMode blocks until the item is dropped and picked up.
hypothesis: Crafting creates the inventory entry without the initialization/event path that attaches or activates the object script instance.
next: Craft a minimal scripted item with an incrementing variable, compare AddItem vs crafting vs drop/pickup, then trace recipe-menu output insertion against normal inventory insertion.

title: Ballistic projectiles ignore defined water impact decals
summary: Non-hitscan projectiles using full ballistic flight modeling reportedly fail to use water impact decals even when the impact data set defines them.
hypothesis: The ballistic collision path bypasses or misclassifies the water-material impact branch used by hitscan projectiles.
next: Create matched hitscan and ballistic weapons using the same impact data, reproduce at controlled water surfaces, then compare impact-dispatch call paths.

title: Moveable objects can warp to worldspace coordinates (0,0)
summary: Mostly frag mines are reported to warp to worldspace (0,0) when cells two grids away are loaded for the first time.
hypothesis: A cell-transition or Havok handoff uses an uninitialized/default world transform during first-load boundary registration.
next: Build a reproducible exterior grid setup with logged reference positions, find the first-load transition that changes the transform, then inspect cell/Havok registration code.

title: Looping weapon/object sounds survive reload or disable transitions
summary: GECKWiki lists several related lifecycle failures: looping weapon audio can replay after death-load, and disabled objects can continue emitting looping sounds.
hypothesis: Looping sound handles are not consistently stopped when their owning reference is disabled, unloaded, or reconstructed from a save.
next: Split into weapon-reload and disabled-object repro cases, capture sound-handle lifecycle, and identify the teardown path omitted by the failing transition.

title: SayToDone fails when the speaker is outside the player's cell
summary: SayToDone reportedly does not fire for an actor outside the player's current cell regardless of persistence/quest status. Related Say/SayTo package-result calls can hang when the player is elsewhere.
hypothesis: Dialogue completion notification is tied to the high-process actor/audio update path rather than persistent script/event state.
next: Build two-cell scripted dialogue repro, compare event dispatch with NVSE's SayToDone event handling, then trace completion notification ownership across actor process levels.

title: StartCombatResponse can select the wrong speaker

title: Havok restitution produces almost no reliable bounce

title: Dialogue hit sounds have no cooldown
